Wedding week.
Statement from Brendan Sorsby:

The memo sent today to all NFL teams lets them know officially that Brendan Sorsby has decided not to pursue litigation and will prepare for the 2027 Draft.  The NFL will not discipline him for currently-known prior misconduct, but it retains the right to investigate Sorsby’s conduct beyond what is in the current public filings. The NFL also reserves the right to take college misconduct into consideration in setting discipline for any future violations.

A memo was sent today to all NFL teams saying that the NFLPA and Brendan Sorsby will not be pursuing any further litigation regarding his entry into the NFL—and that instead, Sorsby will focus on his preparation for entry into the 2027 NFL Draft. Sorsby will be considered a “Draft-Eligible” player for the 2027 NFL Draft and will not be eligible to sign an NFL Player Contract until the completion of the 2027 NFL Draft.

A story about Dave that definitely won’t be in the book, because I doubt he knows it even happened: In 2019 I was an intern, and I was struggling to find my footing at Barstool. Was doing a bunch of odd jobs in the video department, but nothing consistently on a major scale. All signs / conversations were pointing to the end of the summer being the end of my internship, and the end of my time at Barstool. That August I saw that Dave, who I had never spoken to at the time, was looking for a new right hand man to replace Frankie, and was going to host interviews to find a new candidate (the same interviews that gave us both Max Dolente and One Month Ethan). I knew that while maybe I wasn’t qualified to take Frankie’s spot, this may be my realest opportunity to sell myself as to why I needed to stay at Barstool. I didn’t tell anyone, but I showed up to the interviews, and pitched myself to Dave. I was terrified, but he told me that if I was willing to put this much effort into a plea just to be at the company, and I had the raw abilities I did at the time, there had to be room for me somewhere. As much as teams want to go star hunting this offseason, this year's free agent class is drying up fast. However, the real secret to building a championship roster isn't loading up on all-stars anymore. It's finding role players at a bargain who make life easier for everyone else. 🔸 Norman Powell As someone who made the all-star team for the first time in his career last season, Powell seems to be only getting better as he enters his thirties. Powell can be the perfect fit for a team with an MLE deal and need a scoring punch off the bench. 🔸 Tobias Harris With Jalen Duren's struggles in the playoffs, Harris was the Pistons second-best player at times. Like Powell, don't expect Harris to sign with a team expecting him to be option A since he's in his early thirties. 🔸 Rui Hachimura Shooting is definitely Hachimura's calling card as he shot better than 50% from three in the 2026 playoffs. Hachimura's capable of having the same kind of production as Harris or Powell but with a lesser price tag and in his twenties. 🔸 Khris Middleton In his 29 games with the Mavs last season, Middleton averaged 10 PPG and 3.3 REBS. Nobody expects him to be the all-star version of himself anymore, but as a secondary scorer and floor spacer, he still has plenty left to offer. 🔸 Mitchell Robinson Thanks to Victor Wembanyama, tall players who can't shoot have a place in the NBA again. With the Knicks most likely letting him walk to avoid the second apron, Robinson is the perfect signing for a team who need interior defense and rebounding. 🔸 Anfernee Simons Small scoring guards don't command a lot of value in the NBA anymore which means Simons can be snagged at a bargain. Last season, he averaged 14 PTS. 🔸 Marcus Smart Smart is the type of player every contender should be lining up for. He sets the tone defensively and the perfect player to have in the locker room. Smart is also a much more reliable shooter these days, making him a more reliable contributor on both ends of the floor. Which free agent is getting way too overlooked right now? 🤔
